title: The eruption that turned day into 60 hours of night 🌋
subject: volcano
description:
Have you ever heard of Novarupta? 👇

In June 1912, Novarupta in Alaska erupted for 60 hours, the largest eruption of the 20th century. Kodiak went dark, and acid ash reached Vancouver and Seattle.

Sources: National Park Service, "The Great Eruption of 1912" (Judy Fierstein); USGS, "Impact of the 1912 Novarupta-Katmai eruption on the Pacific Northwest" (2017); Alaska Volcano Observatory, "Novarupta 1912".

scenes.text: A lantern held at arm's length could barely be seen.
Kodiak, Alaska, June 1912. It stayed that dark for 60 hours, and a foot of ash buried the town.
Novarupta, a volcano 100 miles away, had blown out about 13 cubic kilometers of magma, the largest eruption of the 20th century.
The ash reached Vancouver. There, white linen fell to pieces when people ironed it.
In 1916, explorers found the valley still steaming and named it the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes.
